✈️ Telegram Command Bridge

Message your Telegram bot — a headless Claude Code agent runs on your machine with real tools and replies with the result.
Not a chatbot — an operator's remote control for their own computer. Long-poll daemon, file-based inbox/outbox, a supervisor that keeps it alive 24/7, and replies that carry the actual result of real work — or an honest failure.

telegram · command-channel · headless-agent · remote-control · self-hosted

--- ## What it is ``` your message -> tg-daemon (long-poll) -> inbox.jsonl -> tg-watch (fs.watch) -> tg-agent -> headless `claude -p` WITH FULL TOOLS -> outbox.jsonl -> your phone ``` The agent does the work (run a command, read a file, edit code, query an API) and replies with the RESULT — or an honest failure. Never a canned "working on it" receipt. ## Requirements - Node 18+ - The `claude` CLI installed and authenticated ([Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)) - A Telegram account ## Quick start 1. In Telegram, message **@BotFather** -> `/newbot` -> copy the token (looks like `123456789:AA...`). 2. `node tg-setup.cjs ` — validates the token, then waits for you to message the bot and auto-discovers your chat ID. Writes `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` + `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` into `.env` (merged). 3. `node tg-watch.cjs` — the supervisor: keeps the daemon alive and spawns the agent on each message. Then just text your bot. ## See it run

--- ## Files | file | role | |---|---| | `tg-setup.cjs` | one-time link: validate token, discover chat ID, write `.env` | | `tg-daemon.cjs` | long-poll bridge: inbound -> `inbox.jsonl`, sends `outbox.jsonl` | | `tg-watch.cjs` | supervisor: restarts a dead daemon + spawns the agent on new messages | | `tg-agent.cjs` | THE agent: runs headless `claude` on your message, replies with real work | | `tg-selftest.cjs` | honest health report | ## Concepts | Concept | Meaning | |---|---| | **Long-poll daemon** | tg-daemon.cjs holds the Telegram connection: inbound → inbox.jsonl, outbox.jsonl → sends. No webhook, no public IP. | | **Supervisor** | tg-watch.cjs keeps the daemon alive and spawns the agent the moment a message lands. | | **Headless agent** | tg-agent.cjs runs claude -p with full tools on your machine — the reply is the result of real work. | | **Setup handshake** | tg-setup.cjs validates the bot token, auto-discovers your chat ID from your first message, and writes .env. | | **Honest failure** | If the work fails, the reply says exactly what failed — never a fake 'working on it'. | | **Self-test** | tg-selftest.cjs reports token, chat, daemon, and agent health without pretending. | --- ## Design notes - **Replies are real work or an honest failure — never a canned receipt.** A reply that claims work is happening while nothing runs is the failure mode this project exists to kill. - **Health is earned.** `daemon_healthy` is true only if a real `getMe()` round trip succeeded in the last 5 minutes, recorded as evidence. A status file that certifies itself is worthless. - **Strangers are ignored.** Your bot's @username is public; the daemon drops every message whose chat ID isn't yours. - **Replies are never truncated.** Telegram caps text at 4096 chars; the daemon splits on newline boundaries. - **Hard tool denials bind even with permissions bypassed.** `DISALLOWED_TOOLS` (git push, rm -rf, sudo, shutdown, reboot) are denied out of the box — the `claude` CLI honors them even under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Extend via `TG_AGENT_EXTRA_DENY`; empty the list only on a machine you fully control (full orchestration). ## Config | env var | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | — | BotFather token (written by tg-setup) | | `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` | — | your chat ID (auto-discovered by tg-setup) | | `CLAUDE_BIN` | (PATH scan) | absolute path to the `claude` binary if not on PATH | | `TG_AGENT_WALL_MS` | `900000` | per-run wall timeout (kills the whole process tree) | | `TG_AGENT_ACK_AFTER_MS` | `10000` | send an honest "still running" note only if a run outlasts this | | `TG_AGENT_MAX_ROUNDS` | `5` | max message batches drained per spawn (mid-run arrivals) | | `TG_AGENT_EXTRA_DENY` | — | comma-separated extra deny globs, e.g. `Bash(docker*),Write(/etc/*)` | | `TG_SETUP_WAIT_MS` | `1800000` | how long tg-setup waits for your first message | ## 24/7 on Windows (optional) Task Scheduler as the mutex — Daily trigger + 5-min repetition, drop overlaps: ```powershell $a = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "node" -Argument "tg-watch.cjs" -WorkingDirectory "C:\path\to\telegram-command-bridge" $t = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 12:00AM $t.Repetition = (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At 12:00AM -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 5) -RepetitionDuration (New-TimeSpan -Days 1)).Repetition $s = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -MultipleInstances IgnoreNew -ExecutionTimeLimit ([TimeSpan]::Zero) Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName "TelegramBridge" -Action $a -Trigger $t -Settings $s ``` ## License MIT — see LICENSE.
